name: Machine learning smart carry (Filippou, Rapach, Taylor, Zhou)

origin.source_title: Exchange Rate Prediction with Machine Learning and a Smart Carry Trade Portfolio (CEPR DP15305, SSRN 3696388)

how_it_works.simple: The normal carry trade buys money that pays high interest. This version also asks a computer model whether each currency is likely to rise or fall, and adds that guess before deciding what to buy.
how_it_works.analogy: Like choosing a savings account by its interest rate but also checking whether the bank looks shaky before you deposit.
how_it_works.precise: Forecast monthly USD exchange rate changes with a panel elastic net (and neural nets) on 70 predictors: 10 country characteristics (inflation, interest rate, unemployment gap, valuation differentials and others) interacted with 6 global variables (uncertainty indices, geopolitical risk, global FX volatility, illiquidity, correlation). Expected excess return equals the interest differential plus the forecast currency change, and a mean-variance investor (risk aversion 5) allocates across currencies monthly.

rule: Each month, re-estimate the panel elastic net on an expanding window, forecast next month's spot change for each currency, set expected excess return = bill yield differential + forecast appreciation, and hold mean-variance optimal weights (risk aversion 5) for one month.
data_needed: Monthly spot exchange rates vs USD for G10 (and legacy euro-area currencies)
Country macro data: inflation, unemployment gap, equity valuation ratios
Global variables: economic and monetary policy uncertainty indices, geopolitical risk index, FX volatility and liquidity measures
economic_rationale: Plain carry ignores predictable currency moves; adding forecasts that react to global risk conditions (for example the dollar's safe-haven moves in 2008) improves allocations (Filippou, Rapach, Taylor and Zhou 2021).
why_it_might_fail: Many predictors and hyperparameters create overfitting risk; the authors show plain OLS on the same predictors loses money out of sample. Results are from a single working paper with no live track record found.

reported_results.source: Filippou et al. July 2021 draft, Table 3 Panel A
reported_results.market: G10 plus legacy euro-area currencies vs USD
reported_results.notes: Smart-Opt ensemble. Basic-Opt (carry only) had Sharpe 0.66; a conventional quintile carry sort had 0.33. With 75% of Datastream quoted bid-ask spreads, Smart-Opt Sharpe ratios are 0.64.

reported_results.source: Filippou et al. July 2021 draft, Table 3 Panel C
reported_results.notes: Smart-Opt ensemble after the financial crisis; Basic-Opt carry Sharpe 0.15 and conventional carry -0.08 in the same period.

post_publication_evidence: No independent post-publication test found. The paper itself notes conventional carry deteriorated after 2008, in line with Hutchinson et al. (2022, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.irfa.2022.102245).

relevance.reason: Combines carry with macro and news-type uncertainty indices, close to parity's thesis, and most inputs (FRED, policy uncertainty indices) are free.
